---
title: "Parameters"
---

EvoDAG is configured with keyword arguments: to `EvoDAGE`, to
`EvoDAG.model.EvoDAG`, to `RGP.init`, and, as a JSON object, to
`EvoDAG-train --kw`. This page lists them, what they do and the value they
have in the default configuration. For the meaning of terms such as the
validation split or the early stopping individual see
[How it works](how-it-works.qmd).

## Where the values come from

When you create a model, its parameters are taken from three places, each one
overriding the previous:

1. the default configuration, a JSON file inside the package:
   `default_parameters.json` for classification and `default_parameters_r.json`
   for regression (`classifier=False`);
2. a JSON file of your own, if you pass `params_fname` (or `-P` on the command
   line). It can be a single object, or a list of objects as the one written
   by `EvoDAG-params`, in which case the first one is used;
3. the keyword arguments of the call.

Keep in mind two exceptions. `EvoDAGE` has its own `time_limit` argument,
which is `None` (no limit) unless you set it, and which replaces the
`time_limit` of the file; a single model uses the one in the file. And the
function parameters (below) are not passed one by one to the engine: they are
converted into its function set.

The values below are those of `default_parameters.json`, the classification
configuration. Where `default_parameters_r.json` differs it is said.

## The function set

There is one parameter for every function that EvoDAG can use to build an
individual. They are written with the name of the function, capitalised. A
boolean switches the function on or off; an integer gives the number of
arguments that the function takes (a function that takes several arguments
uses *up to* that many) and `0` switches it off.

| Function | Meaning | Default |
|:-------------|:-----------------------------------------|:-------------------|
| `Add` | sum of its arguments, with least-squares coefficients | 60 arguments |
| `Mul` | product of its arguments | 20 |
| `Min`, `Max` | element-wise minimum, maximum of the arguments | 5 each |
| `Hypot` | $\sqrt{a^2 + b^2}$ of two arguments | 2 |
| `Atan2`, `Div` | arctangent of the quotient, and quotient, of two arguments | `Atan2` 0, `Div` false |
| `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` | Gaussian and multinomial Naive Bayes over the arguments (classification only) | 5 each |
| `Centroid` | nearest centroid over the arguments (classification only) | 2 (0 in regression) |
| `Atan`, `Fabs`, `Sin`, `Sqrt`, `Tan`, `Tanh` | one-argument functions | true |
| `Acos`, `Acosh`, `Asin`, `Asinh`, `Atanh`, `Ceil`, `Cos`, `Cosh`, `Exp`, `Expm1`, `Floor`, `Lgamma`, `Log`, `Log10`, `Log1p`, `Log2`, `Sign`, `Sinh`, `Sq` | one-argument functions | false |
| `Argmax`, `Argmin` | present in the file with value 0, but not part of the engine's function set, so a value has no effect | 0 |

In regression `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `Centroid` are not used, and in
the regression configuration they are 0.

## Parameters of the evolution

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `popsize` | 4000 | number of individuals in the population |
| `population_class` | `"SteadyState"` | `"SteadyState"` replaces one individual per step; `"Generational"` replaces the whole population every `popsize` offspring |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | 4000 | the run stops when this many offspring have been created without improving the early stopping individual; a negative value means `popsize` |
| `generations` | `null` | maximum number of generations (a generation is `popsize` offspring); `null` means no limit, and then the early stopping or the time limit ends the run |
| `time_limit` | 3600 | seconds. In an ensemble the limit is shared by all members: a member that finds less than two seconds left is not trained |
| `seed` | 0 | seed of the pseudo-random numbers; the members of an ensemble use `seed`, `seed + 1`, and so on |
| `tournament_size` | 2 | individuals drawn in each tournament, both when selecting arguments and when selecting the one that leaves |
| `random_generations` | 1 | number of generations in which arguments are drawn uniformly instead of by tournament on fitness |
| `unique_individuals` | false | when true an offspring that repeats a function applied to the same arguments is rejected |
| `function_selection` | true | when true the function of each offspring is chosen by a tournament on the average fitness its offspring obtained; when false, uniformly at random |
| `fs_tournament_size` | 2 | size of that tournament over functions |
| `min_density` | 0.8 | when the average fraction of non-zero values in the population is below it, only the functions that keep sparse data sparse are used |

## Parameters of the data and the fitness

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `classifier` | true | classification when true, regression when false |
| `fitness_function` | `"BER"` (`"ER"` in regression, where it has no effect) | measure of the fitness in classification; see below |
| `multiple_outputs` | true | whether the individuals have several outputs. It is always on in classification, where there is one output per class; in regression it is for problems with several targets, and the default configuration for regression turns it off |
| `tr_fraction` | 0.5 | proportion used for training when the data are split into the training and the validation part; see [How it works](how-it-works.qmd#early-stopping-and-the-validation-split). With `1` there is no validation set and `generations` must be set |
| `finite` | true | non-finite values (`nan`, infinities) in the input variables are replaced by zero |

`fitness_function` accepts, for classification: `BER` (the default; the mean
recall over the classes), `ER` and `accuracy`, `macro-F1`, `macro-Precision`,
`F1` (of one class; the smallest one unless `F1_index` is given),
`macro-RecallF1`, `accDotMacroF1`, and variants built from recall,
precision and F1 whose names start with `Dot` or `g_` (the geometric mean over
the classes) or with `a_` (the arithmetic mean). The definitions are in
`EvoDAG/bagging_fitness.py` and `EvoDAG/cython_utils.pyx`. In regression the
fitness is always minus the sum of absolute errors on the training part,
and the validation fitness the negative relative squared error.

## Parameters of the initial population

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `all_inputs` | true | create individuals until every input variable has been used once, instead of until the population has `popsize` individuals |
| `pr_variable` | 0.9 | probability that an initial individual is a single input variable rather than an input function over several variables |
| `input_functions` | `["NaiveBayes", "NaiveBayesMN", "Centroid"]` (`null` in regression) | functions used to build the initial individuals that combine inputs; names of functions among `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN`, `Centroid` and `MultipleVariables` (all four at most) |
| `use_all_vars_input_functions` | true | first create one individual for each input function applied to all the variables |
| `share_inputs` | false | has no effect in this release: the lists of inputs that it is meant to share are rebuilt right after |

## Other parameters of the engine

These are not in the default configuration file, but they are accepted by
the constructors.

| Parameter | Default | What it does |
|:-----------------------|:------------|:------------------------------------------------|
| `negative_selection` | true | the individual that leaves is the worst of a tournament; when false it is chosen at random |
| `orthogonal_selection` | false | choose the arguments by agreement (see [Selection](selection.qmd)) |
| `orthogonal_dot_selection` | false | choose the arguments by a dot-product measure (see [Selection](selection.qmd)) |
| `F1_index` | -1 | class used by `fitness_function="F1"`; -1 means the smallest class |
| `remove_raw_inputs` | true | free the training inputs once the initial population exists |
| `number_tries_feasible_ind` | 30 | attempts to find a valid individual before giving up |
| `probability_calibration` | `None` | a class with the `fit` / `predict_proba` interface of scikit-learn; it is fitted on the outputs of the early stopping individual on the validation part, and then enables `predict_proba` of a single model and the calibrated probabilities of the ensemble |
| `labels` | `None` | the class labels, if you do not want them taken from `y` |
| `max_training_size` | not set | with `n_jobs` greater than 1, each member of the ensemble learns from a random subsample of at most this many examples |

`EvoDAGE` also takes `n_estimators` (30), `n_jobs` (1), `tmpdir` (a directory
where finished members are stored, so that an interrupted fit can be resumed)
and `time_limit`.

## The random search of parameters

`EvoDAG-params` samples configurations from `parameter_values.json`. It is a
JSON object that gives, for each parameter, the list of values that the search
may choose from; one configuration takes one value of each list, and the
configurations are drawn at random without repetition. The sets are:

| Parameter | Values that the search may choose |
|:--------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------------|
| `Add` | 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `Mul`, `Max`, `Min`, `NaiveBayes`, `Centroid` | 0, 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `NaiveBayesMN` | 2, 5, 10, 20, 40 |
| `Hypot`, `Atan2` | 0, 2 |
| `Acos`, `Asin`, `Atan`, `Cos`, `Div`, `Expm1`, `Fabs`, `Log1p`, `Sin`, `Sq`, `Sqrt`, `Tan` | true, false |
| every other function | false |
| `popsize` | 100, 200, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 (only those that do not exceed the size of the training set) |
| `early_stopping_rounds` | 500, 1000, 2000, 4000 |
| `population_class` | `"SteadyState"`, `"Generational"` |
| `unique_individuals`, `function_selection`, `all_inputs`, `use_all_vars_input_functions` | true, false |
| `random_generations` | 0, 1 |
| `input_functions` | four lists: all three of `NaiveBayes`, `NaiveBayesMN` and `MultipleVariables`, and each of those alone |
| `classifier`, `finite`, `fitness_function`, `fs_tournament_size`, `generations`, `min_density`, `multiple_outputs`, `pr_variable`, `share_inputs`, `time_limit`, `tournament_size`, `tr_fraction` | one fixed value |

Combinations that make no sense are skipped: a `Generational` population
needs `early_stopping_rounds` at least equal to `popsize`, and
`early_stopping_rounds` cannot exceed the number of training examples.
Each sampled configuration is trained three times, with seeds 0, 1 and 2, and
the configurations are ranked by the median validation fitness of the three
runs. See [Command line](cli.qmd) for the options of `EvoDAG-params`, and
use `--parameters-values` to search a space of your own.
